items.description: Shares of Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd., the world's largest electric vehicle battery maker, fell more than 8% on Tuesday after the company announced a $5 billion share placement in Hong Kong — the city's largest equity offering this year.

items.description: In a dramatic one-two punch over the weekend, Chinese solar manufacturers Trina Solar and Longi both announced record-breaking silicon solar cell efficiencies above 28%, with each company's result independently certified by Germany's Institute for Solar Energy Research Hamelin (ISFH).

items.title: Colombia summit yields mandate for fossil fuel treaty talks

featured_image.name: The world's first fossil fuel phaseout conference has begun in Santa Marta,  Colombia, with 57 countries representing more than half of global GDP, 30%  of the world's population and 20% of global

items.description: Around 60 countries are meeting this week in the Colombian coastal city of Santa Marta for what organizers are calling the first global conference dedicated to transitioning away from fossil fuels — a gathering that pointedly excludes the world's largest greenhouse gas emitters, including the United States, China, and Russia.

items.title: India's power demand hits record as heatwave and Iran war strain global energy markets

featured_image.name: India's power grid creaks under hybrid work model, heatwave | Reuters

items.description: The Iran war and a punishing heatwave across South Asia are reshaping global energy markets in real time, driving record-breaking demand for Chinese clean technology exports, pushing India's power grid to its limits, and reinforcing Europe's pivot toward renewables.

items.title: BOJ holds rates but 6-3 split signals June hike

featured_image.name: Bank of Japan holds key rate as Middle East war dims outlook

items.description: The Bank of Japan held its benchmark interest rate at 0.75% on Tuesday in a 6-3 vote that revealed growing pressure within the central bank to tighten policy, kicking off a consequential week for global monetary policy with the Federal Reserve set to announce its own decision on Wednesday.

items.title: Iran war energy shock pushes millions back to charcoal and firewood

featured_image.name: DRC's reliance on charcoal threatens forests and fuels armed conflict

items.description: Two months after the start of the Iran war upended global energy markets, soaring fuel prices are forcing millions of families in Africa and South Asia to abandon cleaner cooking methods and revert to charcoal and firewood — a shift that conservationists warn is accelerating deforestation and threatening fragile wildlife habitats.

items.title: Iraq taps political newcomer al-Zaidi as prime minister-designate

featured_image.name: Iraq president nominates Ali al-Zaidi as PM-designate - Le Monde

items.description:
Iraqi President Nizar Amedi on Monday designated Ali al-Zaidi, a 40-year-old businessman and political newcomer, as prime minister-designate, tasking him with forming a new government after months of political deadlock and weeks of fraught negotiations shaped by American pressure.[1][2][3]

The appointment came on the final day of the constitutional deadline, after the Coordination Framework — a coalition of Shiite factions holding around 185 of parliament's 329 seats — endorsed al-Zaidi as its "consensus candidate" following a meeting at the government palace in Baghdad.[4][5]

items.title: Iran offers to reopen Strait of Hormuz, but Trump is dissatisfied with proposal

featured_image.name: Trump 'not satisfied' with Iran's latest proposal to reopen Strait Hormuz,  end the war

items.description: Iran offered the United States a new proposal on Monday to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end the two-month-old war, but the plan — which would defer the core dispute over Tehran's nuclear program — drew a cool reception from President Trump and exposed divisions within his administration over how to proceed.

items.title: First LNG tanker crosses Hormuz since Iran war began

featured_image.name: ADNOC LNG Tanker Crosses Strait Of Hormuz - Marine Link

items.description:
A liquefied natural gas tanker managed by the UAE's ADNOC has crossed the Strait of Hormuz and appeared off the west coast of India, ship-tracking data showed on Monday, in what would be the first loaded LNG tanker to transit the strait since the Iran war began on February 28.[1][2]

The 136,357-cubic-meter vessel was last seen in the Gulf on March 30 before reappearing near India after several weeks without a signal, according to data from ICIS LNG Edge, Marine Traffic and LSEG. Ships in the Gulf have increasingly resorted to evasive tactics, including stopping location transmissions or broadcasting false identification numbers, to avoid being targeted or detained.[2]

items.title: Iran war and record heat reshape global energy markets

featured_image.name: Iranians hold talks with Europeans and U.N. Security Council : NPR

items.description: Two months into the war in Iran, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and a punishing wave of early-season heat across Asia are reshaping global energy markets, driving record electricity demand and accelerating a shift toward renewable power — with China emerging as the chief beneficiary.

items.title: Iran war energy shock drives charcoal surge, threatening African wildlife

featured_image.name: DRC's reliance on charcoal threatens forests and fuels armed conflict

items.description:
In Brenda Obare's kitchen in Kibera, one of Nairobi's largest informal settlements, the blue flame of a gas stove has given way to a charcoal fire. "We don't have many choices," she told the Associated Press. "You make do with what you can afford."[1][2]

Her story is becoming common across Africa and South Asia, where energy disruptions caused by the Iran war are pushing millions of families back to charcoal and firewood as cleaner cooking fuels grow unaffordable. The reversal is threatening years of progress in conservation and public health.

items.title: China's clean energy exports shatter records as Iran war reshapes global demand

featured_image.name: China's solar panel exports to Africa surged in 2025

items.description: The war in Iran has sent oil-starved countries scrambling for alternative energy sources, and many are turning to China, the world's dominant producer of solar panels, batteries, and electric vehicles. New data shows the conflict is accelerating a global shift toward renewables at a pace that has surprised even energy analysts.

items.title: Iran offers to reopen Hormuz as strait traffic grinds to a halt

featured_image.name: US seizes Iranian-flagged cargo ship near Strait of Hormuz as new ...

items.description: The Strait of Hormuz has ground to a virtual standstill, with only a handful of small vessels observed transiting the waterway over the weekend as competing American and Iranian blockades choke off one of the world's most critical shipping lanes. Peace negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain frozen, raising the specter of a prolonged supply disruption affecting crude oil, natural gas, and fertilizers.

items.title: Merz says US is being 'humiliated' by Iran as talks stall

featured_image.name: Germany's Merz: US 'humiliated' by Iran, no end in sight to conflict

items.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz delivered a pointed rebuke of the United States' strategy in its ongoing conflict with Iran on Monday, warning that Washington lacks a credible path out of the war and that the Iranian leadership is making a mockery of American diplomatic efforts.

items.title: Seized Iran-linked supertankers sail west under US control

featured_image.name: US warships used Diego Garcia to capture shadow fleet tanker

items.description:
Two Iran-linked oil supertankers seized by U.S. forces in the Indian Ocean last week are now sailing westward in close proximity to each other, according to maritime tracking data, though Washington has given no formal indication of their intended destination.

The M/T Tifani was boarded by U.S. Navy SEALs on April 21 between Sri Lanka and Indonesia, carrying approximately 2 million barrels of Iranian crude loaded at Kharg Island earlier in the month. Two days later, on April 23, U.S. forces boarded the M/T Majestic X — formerly known as the Phonix — in roughly the same stretch of the Indian Ocean. That vessel, a Very Large Crude Carrier also capable of transporting 2 million barrels, had been bound for Zhoushan, China. Both tankers were seized pursuant to warrants issued by the U.S. Department of Justice, according to TankerTrackers.com.[1][2][3][4][5][6]

items.title: Chinese scientists unveil iron flow battery and zero-emission coal cell

featured_image.name: China: 'World's largest' iron-chromium flow battery set for commercial use

items.description: Two separate research teams from Chinese institutions have announced advances in clean energy technology this month, proposing a near-zero-emission coal fuel cell and unveiling an iron-based flow battery that could reshape large-scale energy storage.

items.title: Adidas shares rise after sub-two-hour marathon record

featured_image.name: 2026 TCS London Marathon - Celebrities

items.description:
Shares of Adidas rose on Monday after athletes wearing the company's new Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3 racing shoe delivered a historic performance at the 2026 TCS London Marathon, including the first official sub-two-hour marathon in history.

Kenya's Sabastian Sawe crossed the finish line on Sunday in one hour, 59 minutes and 30 seconds, shattering the previous world record held by the late Kelvin Kiptum by 65 seconds and becoming the first man to break the two-hour barrier in a sanctioned race. Ethiopia's Yomif Kejelcha finished second in 1:59:41, meaning two men ran under two hours in the same competition. In the women's race, defending champion Tigst Assefa set a new women-only world record of 2:15:41, with the top three women all finishing under 2:16 for the first time in marathon history.[1][2][3]

All three record-setters wore the Adizero Adios Pro Evo 3. Adidas shares climbed approximately 1.2% on Monday following the results, according to Reuters.[4][5][6]

items.title: OpenAI, Microsoft end exclusive IP deal in revised pact

featured_image.name: Microsoft says OpenAI is now a competitor in AI and search - CNBC

items.description: OpenAI and Microsoft disclosed an amended partnership agreement on Sunday that removes Microsoft's exclusive rights to OpenAI's intellectual property and allows the AI company to serve customers across any cloud provider, according to The Wall Street Journal. The revised deal grants OpenAI more freedom while capping the revenue share it must pay Microsoft, marking the latest chapter in a relationship that has grown increasingly complex as the AI industry has expanded.[1]

items.title: Iran's Araghchi meets Putin as US peace talks stall

featured_image.name: Iran FM Abbas Araghchi in St Petersburg after 'productive' Pakistan, Oman  diplomacy

items.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in St. Petersburg on Monday to hold talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, capping an intensive diplomatic tour across Pakistan and Oman as negotiations between Tehran and Washington over the ongoing conflict remain stalled.[1][2][3]

items.title: China blocks Meta's $2B acquisition of AI startup Manus

featured_image.name: Beijing's surprise intervention on Meta's Manus rattles tech ... - CNBC

items.description:
China's top economic planner on Monday ordered the cancellation of Meta Platforms' $2 billion acquisition of artificial intelligence startup Manus, a decisive move to keep homegrown AI technology within Beijing's borders amid an intensifying tech rivalry with the United States.

The National Development and Reform Commission issued a brief statement saying the deal's cancellation was made "in accordance with laws and regulations," according to Bloomberg  and Reuters. The NDRC did not elaborate further. Meta representatives did not immediately respond to requests for comment.[1][2]
